design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST: The customer asks for one thing — settle her denied observation stay without an external review so she is never billed. To do it correctly the agent must (1) read in the external-review close-out that its value waits on the payer's recovery and on the small-item write-off, and that the decision is not recorded until the self-administered drugs carry their write-off; (2) read in the small-item rule that it too waits on the recovery; (3) see in the claim activity that the claim was paid, that the member-level appeal was filed and upheld, and that none of these entries exists; (4) price the refund (net of the released copay), the small items, the drugs and the remaining services from the observation account's postings under Riverbend's Network Health terms; and (5) do them in order and hand the decision to the patient.
SCOPE (rework rounds 2-3): task 1 claims the four policies whose domain is a commercial claim of an Observation Stay or Emergency Department Visit Account — the post-payment refund, the observation and emergency small items, the self-administered drugs and the external-review close-out — and their four tools; task 0 claims the outpatient-surgery policies. The external-review close-out requires a filed member-level appeal and every level used; the member-decision close-out requires that no member-level appeal was filed, so the two roots never meet on one claim (probe: task 0's policies evaluate 0.00 on this world).
DRAW: prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,5,4,6] (multiset): refund 6, close-out 6, small items 5, drugs 4.
PROBLEM TREE: root claim_ext_external_review_decision_closeout (owner=user, close_denial_on_external_review_decision_5747d436). Edges: root <- refund (value_input, recovered): 'The external-review close-out is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim.'; root <- small items (value_input, small_booked): 'The external-review close-out is fixed only after the small items that pass the small-item test carry their below-threshold write-off entry on the claim.'; root <- drugs (state_gate, claim_transactions.writeoff_reason): 'The patient's external-review decision is not recorded until, on an account that carries self-administered drugs and no non-covered patient liability, those drugs carry their non-covered write-off entry on the claim.'; small items <- refund (value_input, recovered): 'The observation small-item value is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim.'. Opening world: claim c0bcf67a-2f7a-44fa-a392-e1beefd60740 holds the billing, the 2026-05-06 remittance (payment 5440.52, CO-45 5160.48, PR-3 150.00), a provider reconsideration and a member-level appeal; no recovery or write-off row. Deletion sensitivity (real tools): skip the refund -> small items 0.00 and root 0.00; skip the small items -> root 2352.50; skip the drugs -> root unchanged 2317.43 but its entry is missing. Permutation drugs, refund, small items gives root 2317.43.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: claim_takeback — claim_recoupment_and_overpayment's gate applies to RECOUPMENT_DISPUTE appeals (policy_scope); the refund rule declares the scoped overwrite of the 'recorded against the remittance that carried it' sentence (sibling of the outpatient-surgery refund; the earliest-posted payer payment, ties broken by the alphabetically first remittance trace number). claim_denial_written_off — one_write_off_per_reason holds; each write-off rule retires the base write-off sentence only for its own items, names every sibling route and restates the base routes. The close-out gate: denied, member-level appeal filed 2026-07-09, 2 appeals >= 2 levels, external review available, 2 whole months since 2026-08-21 < 4 (ACA external review follows the claimant's own internal appeal).
REFUND (4121.86): echocardiogram_contract_fee (parameter) -> 3646.10; ecg_tracings_counted (method) -> 4044.80; retained_lab_pricing (method) -> 3992.70; ct_angiography_family_pricing (method) -> 3096.09; diagnostic_campus_factor (parameter) -> 4044.57; member_cost_share_netting (parameter) -> 3971.86. All-baseline 2096.92.
SMALL ITEMS (12.33): observation_antiemetic_unit_rate (parameter) -> 17.78; ketorolac_pricing (method) -> 19.57; observation_iv_solution_unit_rate (parameter) -> 17.01; saline_flush_unit_rate (parameter) -> 15.86; small_item_campus_factor (parameter) -> 13.70. All-baseline 36.92.
DRUGS (45.00): oral_drug_quantity_share (parameter) -> 78.00; oral_dexamethasone_quantity_share (parameter) -> 49.80; inhalation_unit_dose_quantity_share (parameter) -> 52.20; sad_dispensing_fee (method) -> 43.00. All-baseline 88.00.
CLOSE-OUT (2317.43): observation_pricing_method (method) -> 1912.05; infusion_contract_fee (parameter) -> 2435.08; heparin_unit_rate (parameter) -> 2332.93; medical_surgical_supply_percentage (parameter) -> 2347.11; sterile_supply_percentage (parameter) -> 2342.05; observation_campus_factor (parameter) -> 2439.40. All-baseline 2210.00; opening-world root 0.00.
FACTOR STRUCTURE: sums of disjoint line families at the standard (expected allowed percentage of charges; charges for the self-administered drugs) plus at most one whole-value multiplier; each factor owns one family or the multiplier and reads only records; factor ids are unique across the charter. Multi-source: echocardiogram_contract_fee, observation_iv_solution_unit_rate, observation_pricing_method (payer class AND campus), retained_lab_pricing, ketorolac_pricing, medical_surgical_supply_percentage, sterile_supply_percentage (payer class AND account class), ct_angiography_family_pricing (payer class AND the CT angiography billed; on PPO one per-code rate for scan and contrast, compared with their combined charges), member_cost_share_netting (released cost-share lines), sad_dispensing_fee (account class AND campus). The self-administered drugs are valued only from record facts of the drugs themselves — quantity-dispensed shares of J8499, J8540 and J7613 on the outpatient pharmacy self-pay list (non-decreasing in quantity and in unit charge, never above the charges), and a dispensing fee by account class at a hospital campus (per line of the three drug codes on an Observation Stay Account, one per visit on an Emergency Department Visit Account), with the total never above the drugs' charges — never from the patient's payer class, and the Observation Stay Account class's own rule (no uninsured discount on an insured patient's non-covered items) is applied as a factor of 1. Cross-difficulty: the hospital-account product throughout.
REALISM: the medical-necessity (CO-50) denial ends in below-threshold, non-covered and appeals-exhausted write-offs only; the self-administered-drug exclusion is applied to outpatient (observation and emergency) claims as Medicare Part B does and never to inpatient stays; ACA external review (4 months) follows the member's own appeal; the CT angiography and its contrast are priced as one family (71275 at its per-code rate whether or not a separate contrast line is billed; on PPO that rate covers the contrast and is compared with the scan-plus-contrast charges), and no pricing turns on a calendar-day crossing; no small item is called packaged; laboratory fee schedule amounts are federal figures; everything else is worded as Riverbend's agreement and price-list terms.
SEED: the observation account (10839.00) was billed 2026-04-05; the 2026-05-06 remittance allowed 52% of the covered 10751.00, released the 150.00 copay (paid 2026-05-28, below the 250.00 prompt-pay minimum) and left the 88.00 of self-administered drugs open. The post-payment denial (2026-06-03), reconsideration (2026-06-11, upheld 2026-06-30), member-level appeal under the form signed 2026-07-06 (filed 2026-07-09, upheld 2026-08-21) are seeded. Decoy: the paid 2026-02-10 clinic claim. After the gold path the payer balance is 1835.10 = the contractual remainder for the month-end close.
VERIFICATION: computations recomputed with check_compute's DSL on handling-time worlds produced by the real tools; full gate block green; probes and the all-pairs method table are in the worklog.
user_scenario:
You are Joyce Gerhardt, 58, a school bus dispatcher who lives in Neenah. You are polite, a bit wary of paperwork, and you want this finished today. At the end of March you went to Riverbend Lakeshore Hospital in Neenah with chest pain and were kept for observation from March 30 to April 1; you paid the 150-dollar copay on Riverbend's portal in May. Later your insurer, Network Health, reviewed the stay and decided it had not been medically necessary. Riverbend appealed, and in July you signed Network Health's form so Riverbend could appeal for you a second time. In August Network Health wrote that the decision was upheld and that you could still ask for an independent external review. You have decided you do not want an external review: you are calling to say so and to have this settled so that you are never billed for the stay.

You open by saying who you are, Joyce Gerhardt, that you are calling from your home number 9205550243, and why you are calling: Network Health's last letter says you can ask for an outside review of your observation stay, you do not want to ask for one, and you want the stay settled so you never get a bill for it. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, 1968-07-23, and your ZIP code, 54956; if they need one more detail, the medical record number on Riverbend's letters is RB22803517. If they ask about your insurance, it is Network Health through your employer, member ID NH227049318, group 220917.

You will not request the external review, and you are not going to ask Network Health for anything else either; if the representative asks, that is your answer, said simply. If they explain that Riverbend has some things of its own to settle on the claim first, or ask whether they may go ahead with what they need to do, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. You do not know any dollar figures beyond your copay and you do not question the ones you are given.

When the representative hands the step for recording your decision over to you and tells you the claim reference and the amount to enter, you enter exactly what they told you and read the confirmation back to them. Once your decision is recorded you thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: A payer recovery entry (reason code WO-72) stands on the claim whenever the payer's post-payment denial of an observation or emergency stay has been upheld on appeal and part of the payment is attributable to the services it reached.
edges.policy_source: The external-review close-out is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: the claim's payment of 5440.52 stands against a post-payment denial upheld at both levels, yet the claim's activity holds no payer recovery entry (WO-72)
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: the refund books a WO-72 recovery entry of 4121.86; the close-out limit rises from 0.00 (root 0.00 -> 2317.43)

edges.condition: A write-off entry with the write-off reason BELOW_APPEAL_THRESHOLD stands on the claim whenever a code on the observation and emergency small-item list passes the small-item test and the payer's recovery stands.
edges.policy_source: The external-review close-out is fixed only after the small items that pass the small-item test carry their below-threshold write-off entry on the claim.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: the account bills the listed small items (J2405, J1885, J7050, A4216), each at or below 50.00, yet no BELOW_APPEAL_THRESHOLD entry stands on the claim
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: the small-item write-off books a BELOW_APPEAL_THRESHOLD entry of 12.33; the close-out then leaves the 71.00 of passing small items out (root 2352.50 -> 2317.43)

edges.condition: A write-off entry with the write-off reason NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER stands on the claim whenever the account carries self-administered drugs and no non-covered patient liability.
edges.policy_source: The patient's external-review decision is not recorded until, on an account that carries self-administered drugs and no non-covered patient liability, those drugs carry their non-covered write-off entry on the claim.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: the account bills self-administered drugs (J8499, J8540, J7613 under 0637) and carries no NONCOVERED_SERVICE liability, yet no NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER entry stands on the claim
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: the self-administered drug write-off books a NONCOVERED_NO_WAIVER entry of 45.00; the patient's decision may then be recorded

edges.condition: A payer recovery entry (reason code WO-72) stands on the claim whenever the payer's post-payment denial of an observation or emergency stay has been upheld on appeal and part of the payment is attributable to the services it reached.
edges.policy_source: The observation small-item value is fixed only after the payer's recovery of its payment stands as a recovery entry on the claim.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The refund must precede the small-item write-off (limited to the recovered amount: 0.00 before, 12.33 after) and the close-out (0.00 before the refund); the small-item write-off must precede the close-out (with it the passing small items are left out). The self-administered drug write-off reads neither the recovery nor any write-off, so it commutes with the refund and the small items (order drugs, refund, small items gives root 2317.43, the same as 2317.43); the terminal state is identical because each tool's entry id derives from its own claim, reason and amount and each moves the payer balance by its own amount. The root comes last: its prerequisite sentences place it after all three.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona raises only settling the observation-stay claim on her decision not to request external review. It never mentions a refund, a recovery, the payer's payment, small items, drugs, non-covered items or any write-off; the only line about other work is a passive consent given after the representative explains that Riverbend has things of its own to settle first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Each of the four tools reads the claim only to copy its customer, denial code and payer balance (the refund tool also copies the trace number and date of the claim's earliest-posted payment remittance), then creates its entry and updates the payer balance; none tests whether another entry stands, whether appeals are exhausted, or any amount, and none returns an error for an unmet prerequisite (see refund_payer_recovery_9b1903be, write_off_observation_small_items_ab2aa651, write_off_self_administered_drugs_664aab61, close_denial_on_external_review_decision_5747d436).
